 PETALING JAYA: Malaysian interim football team coach Tan Cheng Hoe believes beating Yemen in their friendly today will be the perfect way to end the Harimau Malaya’s 2026 campaign.
 That, of course, will also improve his chances of landing the job permanently.
 Especially when there are sources claiming that the Football Association of Malaysia are again looking east for their next coach – this time to Japan.
 Malaysia, ranked 135th in the world, have won six, lost five and drawn one of their 12 matches in all competitions this year.
 They are determined to add one more win to that run against Yemen, ranked world No. 147, at the Zhaoqing New District Sports Centre Stadium in Guangdong.
 Malaysia’s best outing came in the FIFA Asean Cup, where they finished third after beating Vietnam 1-0 in the third-place playoff on Oct 5.
 Huge confidence: The national players hard at work during training ahead of the Yemen friendly. — FAM/Malaysia NT 
 Cheng Hoe said his charges will look to bounce back from their 2-0 loss to China on Saturday with an impressive win over Yemen.
 “The defeat to China affected the team’s confidence level somewhat,’’ he said.
 “But with a day or two of preparation, I think the players have gained the best experience and momentum, especially with the team playing so well in the second half.
 “We will continue this momentum, and we also want a victory over Yemen because it will give us confidence for the future.”
 Malaysia last met the Middle East nation in 2014, winning 2-1 in the 2015 Asian Cup qualifiers.
 In five meetings, Malaysia have won four and lost one, the solitary defeat a 0-1 loss in a friendly in 1990.
 On the lessons from the China match, Cheng Hoe admitted the midfield needs work.
 “I felt that perhaps the deficiencies in the midfield affected our ball control somewhat.
 “But it was good that we gave opportunities to the other players as they gained valuable experience at the international level, especially against a China team that are so strong physically and tactically.’’
